text:
ash: Ran a set of nsys traces against the latest dedicated pool to investigate the sudden regression in P99 token latency. first pass attached to the running container, then did an nvprof comparator. seeing weird zero-duration kernels in the timeline.
maria: which nsys version and driver on that node?
ash: nsys 23.5.1, driver 535.101.0, CUDA 12.1. nvprof used for older baseline (nvprof 10.2). trace commands:
```
nsys profile --output /tmp/trace_ns --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite --target-pid=$PID
nvprof --profile-child-processes --log-file nvprof baseline.log ./serve --model x
```
bobby: 0-duration kernels usually mean CUPTI timestamps failed or there was a driver mismatch. check libcupti loaded by nsys in the container mount. also check seccomp/ptrace perms when attaching to docker.
ash: confirmed the container has /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so. But nsys stdout printed: "WARNING: CUPTI - Incompatible CUPTI library version". Later the timeline shows rapid kernel enqueues with no recorded duration, and KV cache lookups collapse into a single host-side burst.
maria: did you try running nsys inside the container vs host nsys attach? sometimes host nsys picks up host libcupti vs container lib and mixes versions.
ash: tried both. host nsys attach -> CUPTI error 9, host-libcupti mismatch. running nsys inside container produced a clean trace BUT attaching to the process inside k8s pod requires CAP_SYS_PTRACE. got EPERM on the attach. had to run privileged debug pod to reproduce.
bobby: that explains it. We had a kernel selection fallback in the runtime triggered by the failed profiling hooks — runtime saw CUPTI attach fail and flipped to a single-thread kernel path to avoid inconsistent perf counters.
ash: yep, timeline shows runtime switching from optimized fused-attn kernel to a fallback generic kernel at t=00:01:12; batch sizes 8->1 for many requests. that lines up with the P99 spikes.
maria: action items: (1) pin nsys + libcupti compat on our perf nodes; (2) improve runtime to not flip kernel selection on profiling attach failures (should use opt-in debug flag); (3) add guard for kv-cache cold path when kernels degenerate.
ash: also noticed that our batching heuristic penalizes requests with small KV cache hits. when kernel changes, the cost model mis-estimates latency and we underbatch. the profiler trace has a useful metric: host-side memcpy stalls before kernel launches — looks like our prefetch path is stalling when fallback kernels are chosen.
perf-bot: trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/trace/1799781234_ns.tar.gz, summary csv attached.
bobby: can someone paste the small nsys timeline snippet where the kernel switch happens? want to share with runtime folks.
ash: snippet:
```
00:01:10.982 cudaLaunchKernel fused_attn_forward 0.234 ms
00:01:11.112 cudaLaunchKernel fused_attn_forward 0.210 ms
00:01:12.045 cudaLaunchKernel generic_attention 0.0 ms  <-- zero duration logged (CUPTI glitch)
00:01:12.120 cudaLaunchKernel generic_attention 1.45 ms
```
maria: that 0.0 ms is the tell. Could also be overhead from continuous batching merging calls; but in our case it's CUPTI.
bobby: for reproducibility, try nsys with env var CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL=1 and CUPTI_LIB path forced: `export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` then run host nsys attach. If that still errors, driver mismatch is the culprit.
ash: I tried LD_PRELOAD in container and host; LD_PRELOAD on host fixed the attach but then nsys crashed when libcupti symbols conflicted with host driver. stack:
```
nsys: /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so: undefined symbol cuProfilerGetState
```
so definitely ABI mismatch.
maria: next steps: coordinate with infra to roll a stable profiling AMI that packages matching nsys and libcupti matching our driver (or use containerized nsys plus CAP_SYS_PTRACE). I'll file infra ticket.
ash: filing now — ticket #INFRA-2291. adding notes about runtime fallbacks and a suggestion to add a runtime flag `--ignore-profiling-failures` default false.
bobby: also add a quick check in our perf test harness: run a short warmup trace and assert all kernel durations > 0 and no CUPTI warnings. that'll catch CI regressions.
maria: agree. also let's add a perfetto run for the end-to-end timeline; perfetto picks up host scheduling wide and can show if our prefetch threads are starving when fallback kicks in.
ash: thanks, will follow up with the trace link and a small repro script. cc @eng-sre for the CAP_SYS_PTRACE change request. :thumbsup:
